findings.message: The last round's blocker is fixed for six named columns, but the same pattern has moved into `keep`. `compliance.evidence_bundle.contents` is personal data: `modules/compliance/server/evidence.ts:28` writes `generatedBy: by(ctx)` and whatever each control's `build()` returns into it. The `keep` text itself says so and defers the problem to '070 follow-ups'. No change owns that follow-up, so erasure and anonymisation still never reach this column. That is exactly what the previous blocker objected to with `KNOWN_UNNAMED`. `keep` was added to the standard for columns with no person in them, and this column has one. Fix: either keep the person out of the signed payload (sign a pseudonymous reference instead), or open a change that owns re-signing or tombstoning the bundle on erasure. Until then, do not list `contents` as safe to keep.
findings.scenario: An Admin generates an evidence bundle, then files an erasure request. `generated_by` is anonymised, but `contents.generatedBy` still holds their actor id and the check-module-standard script passes.

findings.message: The new per-column check only covers columns whose names look personal, plus json/jsonb columns, and only inside tables that already have a personal-named column. It misses the class this round fixed by hand. Free-text columns such as `detail`, `description`, `summary`, `body` and `reason` don't match `PERSONAL`, which is why `career.history.detail`, `it_access.change.detail`, `presales.*.note` and `delivery.deployment.note` had to be added manually. It also skips a jsonb column in a table whose only person column is a pseudonymous `user_id`, even though the comment says jsonb 'can carry a copy of one'. Fix: check every text and json column of any table that has a retention entry or a `user_id`/`person_id`, and require it to appear in `fields`, `subject`, `subjectName` or `keep`. Add these cases to the ac7-config table.
findings.scenario: A migration adds `create table x.audit (id uuid, user_id uuid, before jsonb)`, or `alter table time.week add column detail text`. check-module-standard reports nothing, and the copied note is never erased.

findings.message: This is still an instance fix of the round-1 B2 finding. The test now builds real cookies, but it still calls `config.events.signIn` by hand with an Auth.js message it constructs itself (`account: { amax }` / `user: { amax }`). Two things the fix depends on remain unexercised. First, that Auth.js fires `events.signIn` after `callbacks.signIn` has put `amax` on the Entra account. Second, that `apps/web/auth.ts`'s `replaced` (`cookies()` from next/headers) still sees the earlier session cookie at that moment, both in the credentials server action and in the `/api/auth/callback` route. If either is wrong, every case still passes and no session is revoked. Fix: drive at least one real sign-in through the Auth.js handler. For example, POST to `/api/auth/callback/password` with an earlier session cookie, and run an Entra callback against a mocked token endpoint. Then assert that the earlier session row has ended.
findings.scenario: Auth.js stops copying `account.amax` into the event, or `cookies()` returns the new token in the route handler. The earlier session stays alive, and every case in switch.test.ts stays green.

findings.message: An unknown `before` cursor reads as the end of the list. The filter `(c.created_at, c.id) < (select … where b.id = ${f.before})` compares against NULL when the id doesn't exist, isn't visible under RLS, or was garbled by the model. No row matches, and `pageRequests` returns `{ requests: [], truncated: false }`, which says 'no older requests'. Fix: look the cursor row up first, and refuse with a ValidationError ('unknown before cursor') when it is missing, instead of returning an empty, complete page.
findings.scenario: get_change_requests is called with `{ status: 'declined', before: <random uuid> }`. The result is `{ requests: [], truncated: false }`, and the model tells the approver there are no older requests.

findings.message: `failureNote` is still a second classifier of which errors are safe to show, and it disagrees with the rest of the app. `packages/api/src/rest.ts:18-20` treats `ToolError`, `ForbiddenError`, `ScopeError` and `ValidationError` as user-facing. Bulk accepts a new `Refusal` class instead, and it drops `ToolError` (which this module's own `refuse` in card.ts throws) and `ForbiddenError`. The fix the finding asked for was to use the existing classes, `ToolError` or `ValidationError`. Fix: throw `ToolError` / `ValidationError` from `decide` and `writeRemind`, delete `Refusal`, and use one shared predicate in both places.
findings.scenario: approve_week over REST on an already-approved week: `decide` throws `Refusal`, which rest.ts doesn't know, so it returns a 500 with no message. The same week in approve_weeks shows '2026-W42 is already approved'. And a `ToolError` or `ForbiddenError` thrown in the bulk loop shows only 'couldn't be done (reference …)'.

findings.message: The cursor is `rows[PAGE - 1].id`, a raw SQL row, before `reviews()` has filtered it. When the scope superset fetched a request outside the viewer's chain, the response gives that request's id to a viewer who may not see it. Fix: use the id of the last row on the page only if it passed the filter, or use an opaque `(created_at, id)` cursor.
findings.scenario: An engineer assigned to Fleet Tracker (not an approver) pages requests. Row 50 is a teammate's request they can't review, and its id comes back as `before`.
